key_insight: A low-code platform that coordinates multiple LLM agents under a Bayesian adversarial framework can reduce error propagation and increase reliability when automating scientific code generation.
problem_solved: Addresses unreliable LLM-generated scientific code, cascading errors in multi-agent workflows, and the lack of principled evaluation/uncertainty handling for AI-for-Science tasks.
method: Coordinate three LLM-based agents (explicit Task Manager to structure user intent, a Code-Generation agent, and an Adversarial/Validation agent) in an iterative pipeline.
Use a Bayesian belief model to track agent uncertainty and aggregate posterior estimates, guiding when to request revisions or trigger adversarial tests.
Integrate the multi-agent loop into a low-code platform that supports iterative debugging, provenance, and domain-aware evaluation for ill-defined success metrics.
impact: Makes LLM-driven scientific coding more trustworthy and practical, reducing human debugging load and enabling reproducible, uncertainty-aware workflows for AI/ML practitioners in scientific domains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing Task Manager → Code Generator → Validator with Bayesian belief arcs between agents
Before/after flowchart illustrating error propagation reduced by adversarial validation and Bayesian arbitration

paper_title: AI-for-Science Low-code Platform with Bayesian Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework
paper_authors: Zihang Zeng, Jiaquan Zhang, Pengze Li, Yuan Qi, Xi Chen
